The Eras Tour was the sixth [concert tour](/wiki/Concert_tour) by the American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](/wiki/Taylor_Swift). It began in [Glendale, Arizona](/wiki/Glendale,_Arizona), United States, on March 17, 2023, and concluded in [Vancouver](/wiki/Vancouver), British Columbia, Canada, on December 8, 2024. Spanning 149 shows in 51 cities across five continents, the Eras Tour had [a large, cultural and socioeconomic impact](/wiki/Impact_of_the_Eras_Tour). It became the [highest-grossing tour of all time](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours) and the first to earn over $1 billion and $2 billion in revenue.

Announced after the release of her tenth studio album [Midnights](/wiki/Midnights) (2022), Swift designed the tour as a retrospective tribute to [all of her albums](/wiki/Taylor_Swift_albums_discography) and their corresponding musical "eras". Running over 3.5 hours, the [set list](/wiki/Set_list) consisted of over 40 songs grouped into 10 [acts](/wiki/Act_(drama)) that portrayed each album's mood and aesthetic. The show was revamped in May 2024 to incorporate her eleventh studio album, [The Tortured Poets Department](/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department) (2024). Critics praised the Eras Tour for its concept, production, and immersive ambience, as well as Swift's vocals, stage presence, and versatile showmanship.

The tour recorded unprecedented public demand, ticket sales and attendances, bolstering economies, businesses, and tourism worldwide, dominating [social media](/wiki/Social_media) and [news cycles](/wiki/24-hour_news_cycle), and garnering tributes from governments and organizations. This also gave rise to multifarious issues: ticketing crashes that inspired a string of anti-[scalping](/wiki/Scalping_(trading)) laws and price regulation policies; [scrutiny of Ticketmaster for monopoly](/wiki/Taylor_Swift%E2%80%93Ticketmaster_controversy) by US authorities; [diplomatic tensions](/wiki/International_incident) in [Southeast Asia](/wiki/Southeast_Asia) due to [Singapore](/wiki/Singapore)'s exclusivity grant; poor venue management in [Rio de Janeiro](/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro) resulting in [a death](/wiki/Death_of_Ana_Clara_Benevides); [a failed ISIS plot to attack](/wiki/2024_Vienna_terrorism_plot) the tour in [Vienna](/wiki/Vienna); and [a political scandal in the UK](/wiki/2024_Labour_Party_freebies_controversy).

Swift disclosed and released various works throughout the tour: the [re-recorded](/wiki/Re-recorded) albums [Speak Now (Taylor's Version)](/wiki/Speak_Now_(Taylor%27s_Version)) and [1989 (Taylor's Version)](/wiki/1989_(Taylor%27s_Version)) in 2023; editions of Midnights and The Tortured Poets Department; the music videos of "[Karma](/wiki/Karma_(Taylor_Swift_song))", "[I Can See You](/wiki/I_Can_See_You_(song))", and "[I Can Do It with a Broken Heart](/wiki/I_Can_Do_It_with_a_Broken_Heart)"; and "[Cruel Summer](/wiki/Cruel_Summer_(Taylor_Swift_song))" as a [single](/wiki/Single_(music)). [An accompanying concert film](/wiki/Taylor_Swift:_The_Eras_Tour), documenting the [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles) shows, was released to theaters worldwide on October 13, 2023, in an uncommon [distribution](/wiki/Film_distribution) deal circumventing [major film studios](/wiki/Major_film_studios). Met with critical acclaim, the film became [the highest-grossing concert film in history](/wiki/Concert_film#Highest-grossing_concert_films). A [photo book](/wiki/Photo_book) of the tour, [The Eras Tour Book](/wiki/The_Eras_Tour_Book), was released on November 29, 2024. A [behind-the-scenes](/wiki/Behind-the-scenes) series, [The End of an Era](/wiki/Taylor_Swift:_The_End_of_an_Era), and a second concert film based on the Vancouver shows, The Final Show, were released on December 12, 2025, on [Disney+](/wiki/Disney%2B). The tour's accolades include an [iHeartRadio Music Award](/wiki/IHeartRadio_Music_Award) for Tour of the Century and six [Guinness World Records](/wiki/Guinness_World_Records). It also inspired Swift's twelfth studio album, [The Life of a Showgirl](/wiki/The_Life_of_a_Showgirl) (2025).

## Background

/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_-_Reputation_Tour_Seattle_-_King_of_My_Heart_1.jpg[Taylor Swift](/wiki/Taylor_Swift) on the [Reputation Stadium Tour](/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour) (2018), the highest-grossing North American concert tour before the Eras Tour
[Taylor Swift](/wiki/Taylor_Swift)'s last concert tour, the [Reputation Stadium Tour](/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour) (2018), broke the record for the highest-grossing US tour in history.[[2]](#cite_note-4) She cancelled a planned concert tour in support of her seventh studio album [Lover](/wiki/Lover_(album)) (2019), due to the outbreak of the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic) in 2020,[[3]](#cite_note-5) and subsequently released three new studio albums: [Folklore](/wiki/Folklore_(Taylor_Swift_album)) (2020), [Evermore](/wiki/Evermore) (2020), and [Midnights](/wiki/Midnights) (2022). As part of her [re-recording](/wiki/Re-recording_(music)) project to claim ownership over the [masters](/wiki/Mastering_(audio)) of her past albums, she released two re-recorded albums, [Fearless (Taylor's Version)](/wiki/Fearless_(Taylor%27s_Version)) and [Red (Taylor's Version)](/wiki/Red_(Taylor%27s_Version)), in 2021.[[4]](#cite_note-Willman-2022b-6)

During promotion for Midnights, on November 1, 2022, she announced the Eras Tour, which she described as "a journey through the musical eras of [her] career", on [Good Morning America](/wiki/Good_Morning_America) and through her social media accounts.[[5]](#cite_note-Jones-2022-7)[[6]](#cite_note-8) Messina Touring Group, an [Anschutz Entertainment Group](/wiki/Anschutz_Entertainment_Group) (AEG) partner, was the tour's promoter.[[7]](#cite_note-Pollstar-2023c-9) She first announced 27 US shows from March to August 2023, beginning in [Glendale, Arizona](/wiki/Glendale,_Arizona), and ending in [Inglewood, California](/wiki/Inglewood,_California). The [opening acts](/wiki/Opening_act) were [Paramore](/wiki/Paramore), [Haim](/wiki/Haim_(band)), [Phoebe Bridgers](/wiki/Phoebe_Bridgers), [Beabadoobee](/wiki/Beabadoobee), [Girl in Red](/wiki/Girl_in_Red), [Muna](/wiki/Muna_(band)), [Gayle](/wiki/Gayle_(singer)), [Gracie Abrams](/wiki/Gracie_Abrams), and Owenn, each two of whom shared a tour date.[[4]](#cite_note-Willman-2022b-6) Popular demand led Swift to announce eight additional US shows on November 4,[[8]](#cite_note-10) and 17 the following week.[[9]](#cite_note-Willman-2022a-11) A second US leg was announced on August 4, 2023, with Abrams as the opener.[[10]](#cite_note-Kreps-2023-12) [Billboard](/wiki/Billboard_(magazine)) thought that the huge demand contributed to "the most chaos-inducing tour announcement of the decade".[[11]](#cite_note-13)

On June 2, 2023, Swift announced the Latin American shows of the Eras Tour, with [Sabrina Carpenter](/wiki/Sabrina_Carpenter) as the opening act.[[12]](#cite_note-Garcia-2023-14) A third show in [Buenos Aires](/wiki/Buenos_Aires) was announced on June 6, hours after the public sale commenced, due to high demand.[[13]](#cite_note-15) [Louta](/wiki/Louta_(musician)) was announced as an additional opening act.[[14]](#cite_note-16) Additional shows in [Mexico City](/wiki/Mexico_City), [Rio de Janeiro](/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro), and [São Paulo](/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo) were announced on June 12.[[15]](#cite_note-17) Shows in Asia, Australia, and Europe were announced on June 20.[[16]](#cite_note-Dailey-2023-18) From June to November 2023, new shows were added to the tour. In Asia-Pacific, six extra shows were added to [Singapore](/wiki/Singapore),[[17]](#cite_note-19) and two to Australia.[[18]](#cite_note-Williams-2023-20) In Europe, eight shows were added initially,[[19]](#cite_note-Willman-2023a-21) followed by fourteen more,[[20]](#cite_note-Willman-2023b-22) then two in [London](/wiki/London);[[21]](#cite_note-23) [Paramore](/wiki/Paramore) was announced as the leg's opening act.[[20]](#cite_note-Willman-2023b-22) Nine shows were also announced in Canada ([Toronto](/wiki/Toronto) and [Vancouver](/wiki/Vancouver)), with Abrams as the opening act.[[22]](#cite_note-24)[[23]](#cite_note-25) In February 2024, a second show was added in [Madrid](/wiki/Madrid) after the venue's football club, [Real Madrid](/wiki/Real_Madrid), asked [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga) to reschedule their match to cover the "extraordinary demand".[[24]](#cite_note-26)

Several politicians and government officials demanded the tour be brought to their country or city.[[25]](#cite_note-27) Places such as Canada and Chile were expected to be part of the tour but were absent in Swift's announcement on June 20, drawing dismay and demands from fans and officials.[[26]](#cite_note-28)[[27]](#cite_note-29) Across [Southeast Asia](/wiki/Southeast_Asia), fans decried the lack of shows in countries like the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and [Hong Kong](/wiki/Hong_Kong) and demanded the tour be brought to there. In particular, her return to the Philippines had been highly anticipated.[[28]](#cite_note-30) Some journalists and fans opined that unlike venues in Japan and Singapore—the only Asian countries that are a part of the Eras Tour—those in Hong Kong, the Philippines and Thailand might not have the proper infrastructure that is required to host the tour.[[29]](#cite_note-31) In addition, Hong Kong and mainland China [reopened to foreigners much later](/wiki/Zero-COVID) than most other places following the [COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Hong_Kong), which may have affected touring plans, as per [South China Morning Post](/wiki/South_China_Morning_Post).[[30]](#cite_note-32) In Malaysia, legal [opposition to LGBT rights](/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Malaysia) and the ban on pop concerts during [Ramadan](/wiki/Ramadan) were cited as potential reasons.[[31]](#cite_note-33)[[32]](#cite_note-34)[[33]](#cite_note-35)

## Ticket sales

Ticket sales for the Eras Tour were handled by various [ticketing agencies](/wiki/Primary_ticket_outlet) around the world, such as [Ticketmaster](/wiki/Ticketmaster), over several dates. Met with unprecedented, record-setting demand, tickets at every venue sold out in hours.[[34]](#cite_note-20_Minuten-2023-36)[[35]](#cite_note-Ong-2023-37) Sales faced technical malfunctions in many countries; bulk purchases of tickets by [scalpers](/wiki/Scalping_(trading)) and [bots](/wiki/Internet_bot) were reported at numerous venues, resulting in tickets being listed on [resale platforms](/wiki/Ticket_resale) for exorbitant prices.[[36]](#cite_note-Roeloffs-38)[[37]](#cite_note-AsianFans-BBC-39) [StubHub](/wiki/StubHub) noted that the Eras Tour ticket sales were "tracking to be the best-selling of any artist [they've] seen".[[38]](#cite_note-40) Jay Marciano, CEO of AEG, stated that Swift outright refused to impose [dynamic pricing](/wiki/Dynamic_pricing) on the tickets in the purview of her fans.[[39]](#cite_note-41)

### US and Canada

- See also: [Taylor Swift–Ticketmaster controversy](/wiki/Taylor_Swift%E2%80%93Ticketmaster_controversy)
The first US leg was set to go on sale to the general public on November 18, 2022. Due to Swift's multi-year partnership with [Capital One](/wiki/Capital_One), their cardholders had [presale](/wiki/Presales) access, which was set to begin on November 15.[[40]](#cite_note-42) Fans registered for the Ticketmaster Verified Fan program from November 1 through 9 to receive a presale code that granted exclusive access to the TaylorSwiftTix Presale on November 15; those who purchased merchandise from Swift's website received "boosts", and previous Lover Fest ticket holders also received preferred access to the presale if they registered using the same Ticketmaster account.[[41]](#cite_note-43)[[42]](#cite_note-44) Swift confirmed ticket prices in advance, abandoning the "platinum ticket" model; they ranged from US$49 to $449, while VIP packages ranged from $199 to $899.[[4]](#cite_note-Willman-2022b-6) According to Ticketmaster, the TaylorSwiftTix Presale provided "the best opportunity to get more tickets into the hands of fans who want to attend the show" by evading bots and scalpers.[[43]](#cite_note-45) It also noted that if demand from the program "exceeds supply", it is possible that "verified fans may be selected at random to participate in the presale."[[44]](#cite_note-46) It later reported that it received a record 3.5 million verified fan registrations for the Eras Tour.[[45]](#cite_note-47) Ahead of the second leg's presale on August 11, Ticketmaster estimated that 14 million users were vying for roughly 625,000 tickets.[[46]](#cite_note-48)
Ticketmaster handled the Canadian sales as well, using the Verified Fan program.[[10]](#cite_note-Kreps-2023-12) Members of the [Royal Bank of Canada](/wiki/Royal_Bank_of_Canada)'s Avion Rewards program received exclusive access to a separate presale.[[47]](#cite_note-49) An estimated 31 million people registered for the Toronto Verified Fan presale, equal to over 77 percent of Canada's population.[[48]](#cite_note-50)

### Latin America

Latin American tickets went on sale in early June 2023.[[12]](#cite_note-Garcia-2023-14) Presale access was granted to [Banco Patagonia](/wiki/Banco_Patagonia) clients in Argentina on June 5;[[49]](#cite_note-51) around one million customers were reported to have queued for the 24,000 available presale tickets for the Buenos Aires shows,[[50]](#cite_note-52) and over three million during the general sale.[[51]](#cite_note-53)[[52]](#cite_note-54) DF Entertainment served as Swift's tour promotion partner in Argentina; CEO Diego Finkelstein called the demand "unprecedented",[[53]](#cite_note-55) based on which [Perfil](/wiki/Perfil) opined that Swift could fill the stadium 36 times if she wanted to.[[54]](#cite_note-56) On the day of the show, more than 1 million users tried to get last-minute seats.[[55]](#cite_note-57)
In Mexico, ticket presale was handled by Ticketmaster's Verified Fan program; registrations ran from June 2 through June 7, followed by a general public on-sale.[[56]](#cite_note-58) In Brazil, previous Lover Fest ticket holders and C6 Bank [Mastercard](/wiki/Mastercard) holders gained access to presales on June 6 and 10, respectively. Instantly after the announcement of the shows on June 2, people camped outside [Allianz Parque](/wiki/Allianz_Parque) to purchase physical tickets to the São Paulo shows that would not go on sale to the general public until June 12.[[57]](#cite_note-59)[[58]](#cite_note-60) The Mastercard presale tickets sold out in 30 minutes, with over one million customers queueing.[[59]](#cite_note-61) On June 12, over two million users queued for the general sale online.[[60]](#cite_note-62)

### Asia-Pacific

Tickets in Japan were sold by [Lawson](/wiki/Lawson_(store)) under their [Loppi](/wiki/Loppi_(ticketing_system)) ticket system. Unlike other countries, all Japanese tickets were only sold as lottery tickets. The pre-sale for [American Express](/wiki/American_Express) card holders began from June 23 to 26, 2023, and pre-sale for Lawson began from June 27 to July 10.[[61]](#cite_note-63) Due to the high demand, Lawson announced the second lottery pre-sale, which began from July 28 to August 3.[[62]](#cite_note-64) The additional general sale took place on August 22, 2023, and immediately sold out.[[63]](#cite_note-65)
In Australia, tickets were only available via [Ticketek](/wiki/Ticketek).[[64]](#cite_note-66) [Guardian Australia](/wiki/Guardian_Australia) reported that the Australian leg was met with unprecedented demand as well.[[65]](#cite_note-Cassidy-2023-67) Within 12 hours, over one million people signed up for presale codes.[[66]](#cite_note-68) American Express cardholders purchased VIP packages from June 26 to 28; the website crashed within half an hour, and all packages sold out on June 26.[[67]](#cite_note-69) Following the scalping highlighted by Australian consumer organization [Choice](/wiki/Choice_(Australian_consumer_organisation)), the [Victoria State Government](/wiki/Victoria_State_Government) declared the Eras Tour in Melbourne a "major event", a legal provision penalizing scalping and misleading advertisement in [Victoria](/wiki/Victoria_(state)). Because reselling a ticket for more than 10% above the original price had already been illegal in [New South Wales](/wiki/New_South_Wales), [the government](/wiki/Government_of_New_South_Wales) investigated the ticket resale platform [Viagogo](/wiki/Viagogo) after the scalping reports. On June 28, those registered with [Frontier Touring Company](/wiki/Frontier_Touring_Company) gained access to a presale for which over four million users queued, setting a national record; tickets sold out within three hours. Ticketek stated it neutralized over 500 million bot purchase attempts during the presale. The public on-sale began on June 30, with tickets selling out that day.[[65]](#cite_note-Cassidy-2023-67)[[68]](#cite_note-70)[[69]](#cite_note-71) A second sale on November 10 sold out within two hours for Sydney and under one hour for Melbourne.[[70]](#cite_note-72) A third sale for a limited number of tickets, including restricted view seats, occurred on February 13, 2024.[[71]](#cite_note-73)
For the Singaporean shows, [United Overseas Bank](/wiki/United_Overseas_Bank) (UOB) cardholders in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam had presale access on July 5, 2023, with over one million users in the virtual queue. [The Straits Times](/wiki/The_Straits_Times) reported that Swift's fans in Singapore and other eligible [Southeast Asian](/wiki/Southeast_Asia) countries began "scrambling" to sign up for UOB cards.[[72]](#cite_note-74)[[73]](#cite_note-75) Around 22 million users registered for access to the 330,000 available tickets during the July 7 general sale, which happened both virtually and via [Singapore Post](/wiki/Singapore_Post) offices; tickets sold out immediately despite website crashes.[[35]](#cite_note-Ong-2023-37)[[37]](#cite_note-AsianFans-BBC-39)[[74]](#cite_note-76) Klook, an official experience partner for the Singapore leg, sold travel packages along with tickets, which were purchased by dozens of Filipino fans and instantly sold out.[[75]](#cite_note-77) [Marina Bay Sands](/wiki/Marina_Bay_Sands) sold tickets coupled with hotel stays and other experiences.[[76]](#cite_note-78)

### Europe

The [Lisbon](/wiki/Lisbon) shows went on sale on July 12 and 27, 2023, via [See Tickets](/wiki/See_Tickets), with transferrable access codes mailed to registered users, who were limited to four tickets per code.[[77]](#cite_note-79)[[78]](#cite_note-80) Standard tickets for both shows sold out within 2.5 hours.[[79]](#cite_note-81) Following popular demand for an additional show in Madrid, Spain, La Liga approved football club Real Madrid's request to move their match from May 26 to May 25, 2024, to make way for a second Eras Tour show at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium) on May 29.[[80]](#cite_note-82)[[81]](#cite_note-83)
Three million people queued for tickets in Germany,[[82]](#cite_note-84) and 600,000 registered for the [Warsaw](/wiki/Warsaw) shows.[[83]](#cite_note-85) All 170,000 tickets for the three [Vienna](/wiki/Vienna) shows sold out within a few hours, marking the largest and fastest ticket sale ever in Austria.[[84]](#cite_note-ORF_Topos-2023-86) All 95,000 [Zürich](/wiki/Z%C3%BCrich) tickets sold out within 30 minutes.[[34]](#cite_note-20_Minuten-2023-36) In Italy, two million people tried to access tickets for the two shows in Milan, per Italian organizers D'Alessandro & Galli.[[85]](#cite_note-87)
In France, [TF1](/wiki/TF1) reported the highest demand ever for a presale. Angelo Gopee, head of Live Nation France, stated, "the demand is such that many have found themselves in a virtual queue just to subscribe to the mailing list which, potentially, will open access to the ticket office. From memory, we had never seen that in France".[[86]](#cite_note-88) The Paris presale opened on July 11, 2023, to over one million queued users. Ticketmaster suspended both Paris and [Lyon](/wiki/Lyon) presales within an hour after reports of [login](/wiki/Login) glitches;[[87]](#cite_note-89) they were rescheduled to July 17 to 21.[[88]](#cite_note-90) Over 250,000 tickets were sold for the six French dates, with AEG France executive Arnaud Meersseman estimating Swift could have done twelve shows due to the overwhelming demand.[[89]](#cite_note-91) According to [RMC](/wiki/RMC_(France)), the capacity for the four shows at [Paris La Défense Arena](/wiki/Paris_La_D%C3%A9fense_Arena) was also increased from 41,500 to 45,000, meaning Swift will perform for 180,000 attendees in Paris alone.[[90]](#cite_note-RMC-2024-92)
Ticketmaster and [AXS](/wiki/AXS_(company)) handled the United Kingdom sale.[[91]](#cite_note-93) Those who had previously pre-ordered Midnights were able to access presales from July 10 to 12.[[36]](#cite_note-Roeloffs-38) London's [Wembley Stadium](/wiki/Wembley_Stadium) officials described the demand for tickets as "unprecedented" and noted that waiting times were "longer than usual".[[92]](#cite_note-94) [Cardiff](/wiki/Cardiff)'s [Principality Stadium](/wiki/Principality_Stadium) tickets were pre-sold on July 14. In addition to website malfunctions, [Forbes](/wiki/Forbes) reported widespread scalping of the tour's UK tickets, with immediate re-listing on sites like StubHub and Viagogo for extortionate prices.[[93]](#cite_note-95)[[36]](#cite_note-Roeloffs-38) Viagogo responded that the demand of the tour's European leg is something the company had not seen "since the Beatles".[[94]](#cite_note-96) The UK general sale took place from July 17 to 19.[[95]](#cite_note-97) In Scotland, the [City of Edinburgh Council](/wiki/City_of_Edinburgh_Council) granted organizers permission to increase [Murrayfield Stadium](/wiki/Murrayfield_Stadium)'s capacity from 67,130 to 72,990 for Swift's three shows.[[96]](#cite_note-98) In Ireland, around 500,000 people registered for the [Dublin](/wiki/Dublin) shows.[[97]](#cite_note-99) On account of the website crashes during the UK sale, Ticketmaster announced staggered on-sale times for Dublin on July 20, 2023; tickets sold out in minutes. [The Irish Times](/wiki/The_Irish_Times) highlighted that, unlike the UK, "the practice of reselling tickets above face value has been illegal in Ireland since 2021", so no scalping was reported.[[98]](#cite_note-100)

## Production

The Eras Tour was produced by Swift's in-house tour production company, Taylor Swift Touring.[[99]](#cite_note-101) The company hired around 90 trucks to haul staging, costumes and other equipment for the shows.[[100]](#cite_note-102) Canadian production designer [Ethan Tobman](/wiki/Ethan_Tobman) served as the tour's [creative director](/wiki/Creative_director).[[101]](#cite_note-Gensler-2023-103) [The Wall Street Journal](/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal) stated, the tour is one of the most expensive and "technically ambitious" productions of the 21st century.[[102]](#cite_note-Shah-2023-104) [Interior design](/wiki/Interior_design) magazine [Architectural Digest](/wiki/Architectural_Digest) named the tour Swift's "most ambitious" [set design](/wiki/Set_design) and praised its [worldbuilding](/wiki/Worldbuilding).[[103]](#cite_note-McLaughlin-2023-105)

### Stage and lighting

/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_-_Singapore_National_Stadium_-_9_Mar_2024(1).jpeg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_Minnesota_-_Midnights_act_11.jpg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_MN_-_Red_act_-_3.jpg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_Minnesota_-_Midnights_act_4.jpg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_MN_-_1989_act_12.jpg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_MN_-_Fearless_act_-_2.jpg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_MN_-_Speak_Now_act_-_2.jpg/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Minneapolis,_Minnesota_-_Midnights_act_2.jpgThe production consists of light beams, smoke machines, [confetti](/wiki/Confetti) shooters, coordinated serial lights, [pyrotechnics](/wiki/Pyrotechnics), and hydraulic platforms.[[104]](#cite_note-Pollstar-2023a-106)[[105]](#cite_note-Raggio-107)[[106]](#cite_note-McCormick-2023-108) The middle stage has mobile blocks that form different shapes of elevated platform throughout the show.[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109)
The Eras Tour staging is expansive, made of digital displays. It consists of three separate stages connected by a broad ramp:[[108]](#cite_note-Cohen-2023-110) a main stage with a giant, curved [widescreen](/wiki/Widescreen);[[109]](#cite_note-Young-2023-111)[[110]](#cite_note-Willman-2023c-112) a [rhombic](/wiki/Rhombus) middle stage;[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109) and a rectangular stage that along with the ramp forms a T-shape at the middle of the floor.[[111]](#cite_note-Horton-2023-113) The stages feature various visuals and effects throughout the show.[[112]](#cite_note-Procell-2023-114) The tour's concept centers on worldbuilding, featuring a diverse set of props and performing styles to convey the varying moods and aesthetics of Swift's albums.[[113]](#cite_note-Aramesh-2023-115)[[111]](#cite_note-Horton-2023-113)
The staging is equipped with an in-built "hyperactive" [hydraulic platform](/wiki/Revolving_stage),[[106]](#cite_note-McCormick-2023-108) with the main and middle stages having mobile blocks that manually rise from the center to form platforms of different shapes,[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109) and another car-like platform that is moved on the middle stage, driven by an operator seated within the platform but concealed from the audience.[[114]](#cite_note-116) The tour's "massive" production is heavily inspired by [Broadway theatre](/wiki/Broadway_theatre).[[111]](#cite_note-Horton-2023-113)[[115]](#cite_note-117)[[113]](#cite_note-Aramesh-2023-115) It was described as a [4D cognitive](/wiki/4D_film) experience,[[109]](#cite_note-Young-2023-111) featuring [pyrotechnics](/wiki/Pyrotechnics), [laser lights](/wiki/Laser_lighting_display),[[105]](#cite_note-Raggio-107) smoke machines, fire cannons,[[104]](#cite_note-Pollstar-2023a-106) indoor [fireworks](/wiki/Fireworks), [PixMob](/wiki/PixMob) LED bracelets,[[106]](#cite_note-McCormick-2023-108) and [image projection](/wiki/Projector) technology,[[108]](#cite_note-Cohen-2023-110) such as [projection mapping](/wiki/Projection_mapping).[[109]](#cite_note-Young-2023-111)

### Music and performance

Designed as a tribute to [Swift's discography](/wiki/Taylor_Swift_albums_discography) across her career since 2006, the Eras Tour covers all of the styles of music that are seen in her 11 studio albums, including [The Tortured Poets Department](/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department), which was added in the European leg of the tour after the album's release. These range from [country](/wiki/Country_music) and [pop](/wiki/Pop_music) to [folk](/wiki/Contemporary_folk_music) and [alternative rock](/wiki/Alternative_rock) genres.[[116]](#cite_note-Barnes-2023-118) Some media outlets dubbed the Eras Tour the "[greatest hits](/wiki/Greatest_hits)" tour of an artist still in her commercial prime.[[117]](#cite_note-119)[[113]](#cite_note-Aramesh-2023-115) The [set list](/wiki/Set_list) placed a somewhat greater focus on albums Swift had not previously toured, including first-ever live performances of several tracks.[[118]](#cite_note-120) According to the music journalist [Alexis Petridis](/wiki/Alexis_Petridis), the Eras Tour is a [musically eclectic](/wiki/Eclecticism_in_music) production, consisting of "dubstep-inspired, dark-hued pop; tweedy folk; monster-chorus-sporting anthems and acoustic guitar-driven songs that show her Nashville grounding".[[119]](#cite_note-Petridis-2024-121)
The concert ensemble included 15 [backup dancers](/wiki/Backup_dancer),[[120]](#cite_note-122) choreographed by [Mandy Moore](/wiki/Mandy_Moore_(choreographer)),[[121]](#cite_note-123) and Swift's live band of six instrumentalists who have been touring with her since 2007 and four female [backing vocalists](/wiki/Backing_vocalist).[[122]](#cite_note-124) Moore was recommended by Swift's friend, American actress [Emma Stone](/wiki/Emma_Stone), who had worked with Moore on the musical film [La La Land](/wiki/La_La_Land) (2016).[[123]](#cite_note-125) To prepare for the tour physically, Swift trained using a custom workout routine designed by personal trainer [Kirk Myers](/wiki/Kirk_Myers);[[124]](#cite_note-126) Swift sang the entire set list daily while running on a treadmill, trained in dance for three months leading up to the first show, and forwent the consumption of alcohol.[[125]](#cite_note-127)

### Fashion

/wiki/File:Eras_Tour_-_Arlington,_TX_-_Reputation_act_1_(cropped).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_performing_%22Enchanted%22_on_The_Eras_Tour_(Tampa,_FL_-_Raymond_Jaymes_Stadium_-_April_2023).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_The_Folklore_Set_Era_(53108930977).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_-_Arlington,_TX_-_Midnights_act_(cropped).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Lover_Set_(53109595289)_(cropped).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Fearless_Set_Era_(53109821975).jpgDesigners such as [Roberto Cavalli](/wiki/Roberto_Cavalli), [Zuhair Murad](/wiki/Zuhair_Murad) and [Oscar de la Renta](/wiki/Oscar_de_la_Renta) custom-made Swift's outfits for the tour to complement each album's aesthetic.[[126]](#cite_note-Regan-2023-128)[[127]](#cite_note-Allaire-2023-129)
Swift's wardrobe at the Eras Tour was a subject of widespread media coverage.[[128]](#cite_note-Friedman-2023-130) Her costumes and those of her accompanying dancers, as well as her microphones and guitars, paid homage to her 10 albums.[[127]](#cite_note-Allaire-2023-129)[[129]](#cite_note-131) They were inspired by previous performances, music videos, and public appearances,[[130]](#cite_note-Cosores-2023-132)[[131]](#cite_note-Wong-2023-133) intended to align with the overarching themes and [palette](/wiki/Color_scheme) of the era Swift referenced in an act, showcasing the various sonic and visual aesthetics she had adopted in her career.[[127]](#cite_note-Allaire-2023-129)[[131]](#cite_note-Wong-2023-133) However, [crystals](/wiki/Crystal) were a unifying fashion choice; costumes of every act were adorned with them.[[132]](#cite_note-Grindell-2023-134)
Attire and accessories were mostly custom-made by fashion houses Swift had worked with before, such as [Atelier Versace](/wiki/Versace), [Roberto Cavalli](/wiki/Roberto_Cavalli_(company)), [Etro](/wiki/Etro), Nicole + Felicia Couture, [Zuhair Murad](/wiki/Zuhair_Murad), [Elie Saab](/wiki/Elie_Saab), Ashish, [Alberta Ferretti](/wiki/Alberta_Ferretti), Jessica Jones, and [Oscar de la Renta](/wiki/Oscar_de_la_Renta).[[126]](#cite_note-Regan-2023-128)[[127]](#cite_note-Allaire-2023-129)[[128]](#cite_note-Friedman-2023-130) Swift wore variations of some costumes at different shows, usually paired with [Christian Louboutin](/wiki/Christian_Louboutin) shoes.[[128]](#cite_note-Friedman-2023-130) Swift's black [fedora](/wiki/Fedora) from "[22](/wiki/22_(Taylor_Swift_song))" was designed by [Gladys Tamez](/wiki/Gladys_Tamez).[[133]](#cite_note-135) Fausto Puglisi, a designer for Roberto Cavalli, stated that he took an "artisanal approach to craftsmanship" while customizing the outfits, claiming "everything must be eye-catching" when designing for concerts.[[127]](#cite_note-Allaire-2023-129) He incorporated [Swarovski](/wiki/Swarovski) crystals in the costumes Swift wore during the [Fearless](/wiki/Fearless_(Taylor_Swift_album)), [1989](/wiki/1989_(Taylor_Swift_album)), and Reputation acts, which required over 170 hours of meticulous "hand-craftsmanship by skilled artisans" to make.[[134]](#cite_note-136) The [sequined](/wiki/Sequin) [tulle](/wiki/Tulle_(netting)) ball gown that Murad designed for the Speak Now act required "over 350 hours of [atelier](/wiki/Atelier) handwork". Ferretti used [chiffon](/wiki/Chiffon_(fabric)) and micro-beading for the Folklore era dresses, while the Midnights Oscar de la Renta fringed bodysuit was hand-adorned with more than 5,300 beads and crystals.[[132]](#cite_note-Grindell-2023-134)
[StyleCaster](/wiki/StyleCaster) regarded the Eras Tour wardrobe as Swift's best fashion collection for a tour.[[135]](#cite_note-137) The New York Times' chief fashion critic [Vanessa Friedman](/wiki/Vanessa_Friedman) considered the Eras Tour a [fashion show](/wiki/Fashion_show) beyond merely live music and praised Swift's "fabulous" but purposeful wardrobe choices for setting the bar high for future concerts by other artists.[[128]](#cite_note-Friedman-2023-130)

## Concert synopsis

/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Lover_Set_(53108816372).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Fearless_Set_Era_(53109813215).jpgSwift performing with her band during the first two acts: [Lover](/wiki/Lover_(album)) (top) and [Fearless](/wiki/Fearless_(Taylor%27s_Version)) (bottom)
A typical show of the Eras Tour lasted 3 hours and 15 minutes. It consisted of between 44 and 46 songs, grouped into 10 acts, representing each "musical era" of her discography. Each act was characterized by a specific [color scheme](/wiki/Color_scheme), costume, and stage design, and transitions between acts were facilitated by on-screen interlude visuals and marked by costume changes with negligible [intermissions](/wiki/Intermission).[[136]](#cite_note-138)

### March 2023 to March 2024

The show commenced with the [Lover](/wiki/Lover_(album)) act. A clock on-screen counted down to show time as [Dusty Springfield](/wiki/Dusty_Springfield)'s "[You Don't Own Me](/wiki/You_Don%27t_Own_Me)" (1964) played.[[137]](#cite_note-Ruggieri-2023-139) Surrounded by dancers in pastel-colored, fan-like tapestry,[[103]](#cite_note-McLaughlin-2023-105) Swift emerged from the platform at mid-stage in a bodysuit and boots.[[138]](#cite_note-Yahr-2023-140)[[113]](#cite_note-Aramesh-2023-115) She opened the show with the chorus of "[Miss Americana & the Heartbreak Prince](/wiki/Miss_Americana_%26_the_Heartbreak_Prince)" leading into "[Cruel Summer](/wiki/Cruel_Summer_(Taylor_Swift_song))".[[139]](#cite_note-Lewis-2023-141) Accompanied by dancers, Swift performed "[The Man](/wiki/The_Man_(Taylor_Swift_song))" and "[You Need to Calm Down](/wiki/You_Need_to_Calm_Down)" in a sequined [blazer](/wiki/Blazer), through a set emulating office [cubicles](/wiki/Cubicle). She then delivered the welcome note with the dollhouse from the "[Lover](/wiki/Lover_(Taylor_Swift_song))" music video on-screen, depicting her various album eras.[[103]](#cite_note-McLaughlin-2023-105) She played an acoustic version of "Lover" on the guitar with her band, backup singers, and dancers,[[140]](#cite_note-Wood-2023-142)[[141]](#cite_note-Bream-2023-143) followed by a stripped-down rendition of "[The Archer](/wiki/The_Archer_(song))" alone on the ramp.[[113]](#cite_note-Aramesh-2023-115) The second act, [Fearless](/wiki/Fearless_(Taylor%27s_Version)), began with the screen showing gold [electric sparks](/wiki/Electric_spark) raining down. Swift reappeared in a metallic fringed dress and country boots.[[138]](#cite_note-Yahr-2023-140) She performed "[Fearless](/wiki/Fearless_(Taylor_Swift_song))" on the main stage, "[You Belong with Me](/wiki/You_Belong_with_Me)" at mid-stage, and "[Love Story](/wiki/Love_Story_(Taylor_Swift_song))" on the T-stage, all alongside her band while her backup singers wore metallic gold and silver jackets and black jumpsuits.[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109)

/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Evermore_Era_Set_(53108854802).jpg/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_-_Arlington_TX_20230331_-_Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do_1.jpgSwift performing "[Willow](/wiki/Willow_(song))" and "[Look What You Made Me Do](/wiki/Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do)" as part of the [Evermore](/wiki/Evermore) (top) and [Reputation](/wiki/Reputation_(album)) (bottom) acts
The third act, [Evermore](/wiki/Evermore), adopted a forest aesthetic.[[116]](#cite_note-Barnes-2023-118) Swift began singing "['Tis the Damn Season](/wiki/%27Tis_the_Damn_Season)" in a long gown,[[138]](#cite_note-Yahr-2023-140) followed by a dark theme that leads to "[Willow](/wiki/Willow_(song))" in a "witchy" [séance](/wiki/S%C3%A9ance);[[137]](#cite_note-Ruggieri-2023-139) she wore a cape and performed with dancers holding luminescent orange orbs.[[130]](#cite_note-Cosores-2023-132)[[138]](#cite_note-Yahr-2023-140) She continued with "[Marjorie](/wiki/Marjorie_(song))",[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109) then "[Champagne Problems](/wiki/Champagne_Problems_(Taylor_Swift_song))" on a moss-covered piano beneath an oak tree,[[116]](#cite_note-Barnes-2023-118)[[103]](#cite_note-McLaughlin-2023-105) concluding the act with Swift introducing her pianist Karina DePiano followed by "[Tolerate It](/wiki/Tolerate_It)" with a male dancer at a dinner table reminiscent of [Citizen Kane](/wiki/Citizen_Kane) (1941).[[142]](#cite_note-144) Snakes visuals and dimming lights started the [Reputation](/wiki/Reputation_(album)) act.[[103]](#cite_note-McLaughlin-2023-105)[[130]](#cite_note-Cosores-2023-132) Swift reemerged in a black asymmetrical [catsuit](/wiki/Catsuit) with snake motifs.[[143]](#cite_note-145) She delivered a high-energy performance of "[...Ready for It?](/wiki/...Ready_for_It%3F)" with female dancers wearing black-dark red gothic [leotards](/wiki/Leotard), "[Delicate](/wiki/Delicate_(Taylor_Swift_song))",[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109)[[111]](#cite_note-Horton-2023-113) and "[Don't Blame Me](/wiki/Don%27t_Blame_Me_(Taylor_Swift_song))" featured light beams and Swift on an elevated platform.[[144]](#cite_note-146) She transitioned to "[Look What You Made Me Do](/wiki/Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do)", which featured on-screen visuals of Swift from all of her eras trapped in glass boxes and dancers dressed in some of Swift's older looks.[[130]](#cite_note-Cosores-2023-132)[[116]](#cite_note-Barnes-2023-118) The act concluded with a snake slithering away on-screen.[[112]](#cite_note-Procell-2023-114)

/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_The_Red_Era_Set_(53109768961).jpgFor the [Red](/wiki/Red_(Taylor%27s_Version)) act, Swift wore a custom [Gladys Tamez](/wiki/Gladys_Tamez) black fedora hat that she presented to a fan from the audience while performing "[22](/wiki/22_(Taylor_Swift_song))".
The fifth act, [Speak Now](/wiki/Speak_Now_(Taylor%27s_Version)), began with an abstract [mosaic](/wiki/Mosaic) of purple lights on the stage.[[145]](#cite_note-Carroll-2023-147) Swift, in a [ball gown](/wiki/Ball_gown), walked in from the screen and performed "[Enchanted](/wiki/Enchanted_(Taylor_Swift_song))" with female dancers; since July 7, 2023, she also performed "[Long Live](/wiki/Long_Live_(Taylor_Swift_song))" with her band.[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109) The color scheme changed to match the next act, [Red](/wiki/Red_(Taylor%27s_Version)); a female dancer opened a box that plays snippets of "[Red](/wiki/Red_(Taylor_Swift_song))", "[Everything Has Changed](/wiki/Everything_Has_Changed)" or "[Holy Ground](/wiki/Holy_Ground_(Taylor_Swift_song))", and "[State of Grace](/wiki/State_of_Grace_(song))".[[137]](#cite_note-Ruggieri-2023-139) Red balloons emerged, and Swift performed "[22](/wiki/22_(Taylor_Swift_song))" wearing a version of the white T-shirt and black hat from the song's music video.[[106]](#cite_note-McCormick-2023-108) Near the end of the song, she greeted a fan pre-selected from the audience, giving them the hat.[[146]](#cite_note-148) Swift sang "[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](/wiki/We_Are_Never_Ever_Getting_Back_Together)" and "[I Knew You Were Trouble](/wiki/I_Knew_You_Were_Trouble)" with male dancers next, dressed in a red-black romper.[[131]](#cite_note-Wong-2023-133) She donned a red-black ombre coat next, and performed "[All Too Well (10 Minute Version)](/wiki/All_Too_Well_(10_Minute_Version))" on a guitar, backed by the band.[[106]](#cite_note-McCormick-2023-108)[[131]](#cite_note-Wong-2023-133) The act concluded with artificial snow falling.[[107]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2023-109)

/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_-_Arlington,_TX_-_Folklore_act_2.jpgSwift in a frilly [Alberta Ferretti](/wiki/Alberta_Ferretti) gown for the [Folklore](/wiki/Folklore_(Taylor_Swift_album)) act, complementing the album's [cottagecore](/wiki/Cottagecore) aesthetic [Cottagecore](/wiki/Cottagecore) dominated the seventh act, [Folklore](/wiki/Folklore_(Taylor_Swift_album)), introduced with a [spoken-word](/wiki/Spoken-word) interlude of "[Seven](/wiki/Seven_(Taylor_Swift_song))".[[145]](#cite_not
